module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 566

*References*:
- [erdosproblems.com/566](https://www.erdosproblems.com/566)
- [EFRS93] Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp, _Ramsey size linear graphs_.
Combin. Probab. Comput. (1993), 389-399.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos566

open SimpleGraph

/--
Let $G$ be such that any subgraph on $k$ vertices has at most $2k-3$ edges.
Is it true that, if $H$ has $m$ edges and no isolated vertices, then $R(G,H) \ll m$?

In other words: if $G$ is sparse (every induced subgraph on $k$ vertices has $≤ 2k-3$ edges),
is $G$ Ramsey size linear?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_566 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin p)),
      (∀ S : Finset (Fin p), 2 ≤ S.card → (G.induce S).edgeSet.ncard ≤ 2 * S.card - 3) →
      G.IsRamseySizeLinear := by
  sorry

end Erdos566

reformulations.difference: The source bounds the edges of every subgraph, whereas Lean checks induced subgraphs on finite vertex subsets of cardinality at least two.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On any fixed vertex set S, every subgraph has its edge set contained in that of G.induce S. Thus the induced-subgraph upper bound implies the bound for every subgraph; conversely, induced subgraphs are themselves subgraphs. An explicit equivalence between the Lean hypothesis and the condition quantifying over every F ≤ G.induce S was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. The restriction to at least two vertices is the intended range of the source's 2k−3 sparsity condition.

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the question. The shared definition uses the ordinary vertex Ramsey number, non-induced copies, a positive constant depending only on G, and all finite H without isolated vertices. Finite vertex types ensure edgeSet.ncard has no infinite-set default-value issue. Lean experiments verified the induced-subgraph equivalence, agreement of natural and integer subtraction for k ≥ 2, positive degree versus non-isolation, and harmless empty-graph cases. Computation accepted K0 through K3 under the sparsity test and rejected K4. The source still records the problem as open. The full EFRS93 paper was unavailable from the attempted archive/publisher PDF links; its defining abstract and both collections' problem statements were accessible and sufficient to verify this declaration.
